captions.linkedin:
CFOs know things public investors don't. The clearest tell is when they choose to issue or repurchase their own stock.

Pontiff & Woodgate (Journal of Finance, 2008) measured this with one number: the log change in split-adjusted shares outstanding. Firms that net-issued underperformed. Firms that net-repurchased beat the market.

The signal beats size, book-to-market, and momentum individually in regressions. That's the headline.

🔹 SPLIT ADJUST, this step is critical, raw share counts lie
🔹 MANAGER TIMING, issue when overvalued, repurchase when undervalued
🔹 CONTINUOUS MEASURE, every firm gets a signed score, not just SEO/buyback events
🔹 ANNUAL REBALANCE, June formation, 6-month data lag
🔹 ROBUST CONTROLS, survives size, BM, momentum, accruals
🔹 POST-1970 ONLY, no effect before 1970, regime-dependent

The regime caveat matters. This isn't a timeless universal law. Pre-1970 the signal didn't work. McLean, Pontiff & Watanabe found mixed international magnitudes. Treat it as a post-war US equity phenomenon.

Pontiff & Woodgate (2008) Journal of Finance; educational only, not investment advice.
